references.text: The same instruction regarding the kidneys, the fat, and the lobe of the liver is given earlier in the same chapter concerning the peace offering from cattle.
An identical instruction is given for the peace offering from small livestock (sheep), where the same parts are to be removed and offered.
For the sin offering, the same rule applies: remove the kidneys, the fat on them, and the lobe of the liver.
For the guilt offering, the same parts—the kidneys with their fat and the lobe of the liver—are to be removed and offered.
At the consecration of Aaron and his sons, the fat, the lobe of the liver, and the two kidneys with their fat were to be burned on the altar.
Moses carried out this instruction at the dedication of the tabernacle, where he took the fat, the lobe of the liver, and both kidneys.
Aaron offered the fat, the kidneys, and the lobe of the liver from the sin offering on the altar, just as the Lord had commanded.
Aaron also placed the fatty portions from the bull and the ram, including the kidneys and the lobe of the liver, upon the breastpieces.
Shows the actual fulfillment of the law from Lev 3:15 during the ordination of the priests.
Connects the handling of the kidneys and the lobe of the liver to the unique ordination ritual for priests.
